title: Atomic theory of matter
summary: John Dalton, working in Manchester, is best known for his pioneering theory of atomism. He presented a series of papers on weather to the city's Literary and Philosophical Society between 1799 and 1801, and developed methods to calculate atomic weights. He published the basic features of his chemistry in 1808, which became the starting point for chemical formulae.

uncertainty.note: Spans Dalton's initial meteorological papers on gases (1799–1801) and development of atomic weights through publication of A New System of Chemical Philosophy in 1808 (completed 1827).

where.modern_name: Manchester, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
where.historical_name: Manchester, Lancashire, Kingdom of Great Britain (later United Kingdom)

importance.justification: Dalton's chemical atomic theory established that elements are composed of discrete atoms of characteristic weights, creating the quantitative foundation of modern chemistry.

related.because: Dalton's concept of characteristic atomic weights provided the ordered physical quantity upon which Mendeleev organized the periodic law of chemical elements.
